messages:
mika: hey folks :wave: i'm mika, started on runtime today. trying to build the inference runtime from source on ubuntu 22.04 with CUDA 12.2 + cuDNN 8.9 and hitting a linker error referencing cublasLt. any quick hints?

jordan: welcome! :tada: can you paste the top part of the error and output of `nvcc --version` and `nvidia-smi`? also `ldd` on the failing .so would help.

mika: sure, pastebin of the compile output (trimmed):
```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12: undefined reference to `cublasLtCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[2]: *** [runtime/libnative.so] Error 1
```

and nvcc/nvidia-smi:
```
nvcc: NVIDIA (R) Cuda compiler driver
Cuda compilation tools, release 12.2, V12.2.148
NVIDIA-SMI 520.61.05 Driver Version: 520.61.05 CUDA Version: 12.2
```

I'm building on baremetal (not docker) and I have libs in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu.

jordan: hmm driver version 520.x might be the culprit — libcublasLt symbols were added/renamed across driver releases. can you `ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so*` and `ldd path/to/runtime/libnative.so`? also check `echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda` just in case.

mika: outputs:
```
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so*
-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 123456 Jul 10  /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so.12
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root      19 Jul 10  /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublasLt.so -> libcublasLt.so.12
$ echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH

$ readlink -f /usr/local/cuda
/usr/local/cuda-12.2
```

no LD_LIBRARY_PATH set.

ashley: welcome mika :wave: this reads like a driver/runtime mismatch. driver 520 is a bit old for some of the newer libcublasLt symbols we use. recommended is NVIDIA driver 535+ for CUDA 12.2 stack. two paths:
- update system driver to 535+ (apt package `nvidia-driver-535`)
- or use our dev docker image which bundles the matching runtime: `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rt-dev:cuda12.2` (recommended for onboarding)

If you need a quick hack: avoid static linking against cublasLt or build with a compatibility flag, but that's brittle. better to align driver and CUDA runtime. also run `sudo ldconfig` after driver install.

jordan: another gotcha: if you have leftover vendor packages (like older nvidia-utils) apt might keep old symlinks. check `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/` for stale paths. we also keep a small troubleshooting script at `tools/check-gpu-env.sh` in the repo — runs nvcc/nvidia-smi checks and prints mismatches.

mika: thanks. i'll try upgrading driver to 535 and rerun. quick question: who owns the runtime onboarding doc / install checklist? couldn't find a doc with exact driver versions.

ashley: runtime-setup.md in the docs dir (docs/runtime/runtime-setup.md). i should update it with the 535 requirement. if you open a tiny PR to add the driver version and a note about using the docker image, i'll review.

devops-bot: CI Alert: build/packager failed for branch mika/onboard-cublas — link error reported. (see: https://ci.redwood/example/1234)

mika: ok updating drivers now. will try docker fallback if driver upgrade is blocked by workstation policy. if it still fails i'll ping for an adhoc pair. thanks all! :thumbsup:

jordan: ping @ashley if you want to pair — happy to join too. add me to the PR for quick review. :+1:

ashley: also note — if you go docker route, use the `--gpus all` flag and mount `/dev/nvidia*:/dev/nvidia*` for local testing. i'll add that to the doc.

mika: got it. big help. will report back in this thread after driver update. :)
